description:
1. Obtain a recursive listing of /working and save the raw results to a file named 'listing.txt' in the current directory.  
2. From 'listing.txt', extract all entries whose base name is exactly 'workspace' and record those full paths to 'matches.txt'.  
3. For each path in 'matches.txt', verify it is a regular file (not a directory or symlink) and write the confirmed regular-file paths to 'regular_matches.txt', discarding any non-regular entries.  
4. Create a short 'summary.txt' that records whether at least one regular 'workspace' file was found and, if so, include the first confirmed path; leave this summary ready for the final output step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Confirm that the path "/working" exists and is accessible, and record its resolved absolute path into a file named "target_path.txt".
2. Perform a full recursive enumeration of the recorded target path and save a raw listing that includes each entry's type to "recursive_listing.txt".
3. From "recursive_listing.txt", extract entries whose basename is exactly "workspace", write their full paths and detected node types to "candidates.txt", and remove any duplicate entries.
4. Consolidate "target_path.txt", "recursive_listing.txt", and "candidates.txt" and create a prepared verification placeholder file named "verification_summary.json" (with an entry for each candidate) so the final step can produce the required yes/no output.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Record the current environment state and accessibility of the path /working into a file named "precheck.txt" in a temporary workspace, including a timestamp and basic access notes.  
2. Recursively enumerate all entries under /working and save full paths with basic metadata (type, size, modification time) to "entries_list.txt" in the temporary workspace, ensuring the list is complete and readable.  
3. Filter "entries_list.txt" to extract entries whose final path component is exactly "workspace" and write each candidate's path and reported file type to "candidates.txt", verifying entries are not duplicated or truncated.  
4. From "candidates.txt", produce a concise evidence file "result_prep.txt" that states whether any candidate appears as a regular file and lists the exact path(s) of such candidates if present, leaving the single-word final output to be produced afterward.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary workspace named "temp_workspace" and collect a recursive raw listing of all entries under /working, saving that listing to "temp_workspace/listing.raw".  
2. From "temp_workspace/listing.raw", extract every entry whose base name is "workspace" and record their full paths plus basic metadata to "temp_workspace/matches.txt".  
3. For each path in "temp_workspace/matches.txt", inspect filesystem metadata to confirm it is a regular file (not a directory or symlink), annotate each entry with a confirmation flag, and remove entries that fail confirmation.  
4. Produce a concise summary file "temp_workspace/status.txt" that contains "found" if any confirmed regular-file entries remain or "not_found" otherwise, and leave this summary available for determining the final output.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
